NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers: magnetic_gradient_separation using a fixed-gradient magnetic drum to capture ferrous contaminants.  
Departure: A dual-zone magnetic field with spatially modulated gradient strength that exploits the size-dependent magnetic saturation of contaminants to separate both ferrous and non-ferrous metal particles in a single pass.  
Physics connection: Magnetic force scales with gradient and particle susceptibility; modulating the gradient creates a force threshold where only larger (high-saturation) ferrous particles are captured in high-gradient zones, while smaller non-ferrous particles are deflected by lower-gradient zones, leveraging the physics of magnetic saturation limits.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: F_mag = (χ/μ₀) * V_p * B * ∇B (magnetic force on paramagnetic/ferrous particle)  
Magnitude verification: For a 1 mm³ iron particle (χ≈200, ρ_p=7870 kg/m³) in a 1 T field with ∇B=1000 T/m, F_mag ≈ 0.2 N; for a 0.1 mm³ aluminum particle (χ≈2.2×10⁻⁵), F_mag ≈ 2.2×10⁻⁸ N. The force ratio (≈10⁷) enables size-selective separation.  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
- Components:  
  - Dual-zone electromagnet array (ALREADY-RECORDED: existing power supply from melt pump drive)  
  - Modular stainless-steel capture drums (ALREADY-RECORDED: standard separator drum material)  
  - Variable-frequency gradient controller (ALREADY-RECORDED: PLC from existing extruder control system)  
- Materials:  
  - Neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) pole pieces (ALREADY-RECORDED: standard magnetic separator material)  
  - Ceramic wear liners (ALREADY-RECORDED: standard for melt-contact parts)  
- Instruments:  
  - Metal contaminant sensor (ALREADY-RECORDED: existing XRF spectrometer output)  
  - Melt flow rate monitor (ALREADY-RECORDED: existing flowmeter from melt pump)  
- Procedure:  
  - Install dual-zone drum array downstream of extruder (ALREADY-RECORDED: standard separator mounting)  
  - Program gradient modulation based on particle size distribution (DERIVED: from stated XRF spectrometer data and melt flow rate)  
  - Auto-clean cycle every 10 minutes (DERIVED: from stated production rate and contaminant load)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Same as standard magnetic separator (modular drum design, no new foundation needed)  
- Operability: Same control interface (existing PLC, no additional operator training)  
- Maintenance: Same drum replacement schedule (standard wear parts, no new tooling)  
- Cost class: Same as high-intensity magnetic separators (NdFeB magnets are commodity items)  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Run recycled plastic melt with known metal contaminant mix (10 ppm ferrous, 5 ppm aluminum) at standard production rate. Measure contaminant reduction in output via XRF spectrometer.  
Pass/fail threshold: ≥95% ferrous removal and ≥80% aluminum removal within 1 hour.  
Duration: 2 continuous production cycles.  
Kill criterion: If either contaminant type removal rate is below threshold, mechanism is falsified.  
Validation: Baseline derived from stated XRF spectrometer data and historical contaminant loads.  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: Metal contaminant concentration (stated as the failure-defining threshold). Secondary indicator: Melt flow rate (supplements to account for load variations).  

CONSTRAINT BIND / RISK  
The dual-zone modulation relies on assumed particle size distribution from XRF data; if actual particles are outside expected size range, separation efficiency may drop. This risk is mitigated by the kill criterion.
